summary.oneLiner: EaseMyTrip delivered strong Q3FY25 EBITDA and PAT growth driven by non-air verticals and Dubai expansion, but air booking growth remained muted due to deliberate discount reduction to protect margins, signaling a strategic shift toward profitability over market share capture.

one-line thesis: EaseMyTrip delivered strong Q3FY25 EBITDA and PAT growth driven by non-air verticals and Dubai expansion, but air booking growth remained muted due to deliberate discount reduction to protect margins, signaling a strategic shift toward profitability over market share capture.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +7% YoY (Q3 GBR INR 2,149cr); EBITDA: +20.7% QoQ to INR 51cr (33.2% margin); PAT: +30% QoQ to INR 34cr (22.1% margin); Order book: Not disclosed; Net debt: Not disclosed - no one-offs or accounting distortions called out
guidance: Revenue growth: Targeting FY2026 with 25% non-air contribution (from current 14%); Margin: Maintaining EBITDA margin >30%; Order inflow: No specific guidance; Capex/commissioning: No capex guidance disclosed
segment / subsidiary detail: Air: 86% of GBR (down from 97% at listing); Hotels: 10.6% of GBR (73% YoY growth in nights); Trains/Buses/Other: 2% of GBR (31.9% YoY growth); Dubai: INR 170cr GBR in Q3 (227% YoY growth); Study tourism: New via Planet Education Australia acquisition
growth verticals / optionality: International expansion (Middle East, especially Dubai); Corporate travel digitization (AI-driven booking tools); Study tourism vertical; OLX and CARS24 partnerships; ONDC integration (mentioned but no update)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved to 33.2% in Q3 due to discount reduction from 3.8% to 3.0%; Cost discipline is core to strategy; No inflationary cost pressures cited; Profitability prioritized over volume growth in air segment
capex / expansion: No capex guidance or figures disclosed; Offline expansion via franchisees (new stores in Raipur, Srikalahasti, Bangalore, Jabalpur, Bhubaneswar, Hyderabad) implies modest CAPEX; No mention of tech or infrastructure capex
capital allocation: Prioritizing profitability over growth; No dividend or buyback mentioned; Strategic acquisitions (Planet Education Australia); Marketing spend on sports sponsorships (Big Cricket League, Kho Kho World Cup, WCL Season 2); No equity dilution planned for FY25 per promoter commitment
risks & watch-items: Intense competition from private players burning cash; Air segment growth suppression due to discount cuts; Delayed hotel GBR growth despite seasonality; Promoter stake sales (though denied for FY25); Execution risk in international and corporate verticals; Regulatory risk in study tourism
management quality / tone: Cautious, defensive, and profit-focused; Management openly admits to sacrificing growth for margin; Confident in long-term sustainability; Repeatedly emphasizes bootstrapped heritage and avoidance of 'burn rate' competition; Tone is firm on discipline, slightly dismissive of competitor tactics
non-obvious takeaways: Dubai growth is highly volatile (spurt-flat-spurts pattern) but management believes <5% of potential captured; Study tourism acquisition is a stealth play into high-margin, recurring education-travel ecosystem; Sports sponsorships (WCL Season 2: July-Aug 2025) are not just branding but direct customer acquisition channels
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Competitors are growing faster by burning cash on discounts | Private OTAs (e.g., Yatra, MakeMyTrip private entities) | loser | Medium | EaseMyTrip's disciplined approach may lose market share short-term but could capture market when competitors' funding dries up |
| Promoter stake sales and CEO transition created investor unease | EaseMyTrip stock sentiment | loser | Low | Management reassured no further sales in FY25, but perception risk remains until Q4 results confirm stability |

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as India's Leading Online Travel Platform / OTA, founded in 2008, offering a One Stop Travel Ecosystem spanning flights, hotels, holiday packages, rail, bus, cab, charter, visa and ancillary services.
- Claims 90%+ customer repeat booking rate and 94.97% repeat transactions, cited as evidence of strong brand loyalty and trust.
- Differentiates via a tri-channel distribution model (B2C, B2B2C, B2E) and says it pioneered No Convenience Fee and Zero Hidden Cost pricing.
- Branded as an AI-Powered Travel platform ('AI-Led Innovation') offering personalized, hyper-tailored, cost-effective bookings.
- Describes growth as funded by internal accruals, framing a self-sustaining, low-leverage model versus typically VC/debt-funded OTA peers.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Nutana Aviation -- majority stake acquired in 2022, extending into aviation-adjacent services.
- [Acquisition] Dook Travels, Guideline Travels and Tripshope -- majority stakes acquired in 2023 as part of non-air segment expansion.
- [Corporate structure] Joined the 'Unicorn Club' and listed via IPO on NSE & BSE in 2021 (Scrip Code 543272 / Symbol EASEMYTRIP); incorporated EaseMyTrip Insurance Broker Pvt Ltd (majority stake) in 2024.
- [Board] Board comprises Chairman & MD Nishant Pitti and Director & CEO Rikant Pitti (co-founders), alongside independent directors with senior government/regulatory backgrounds -- ex-CBDT Member Neena Kumar, ex-CCI Director General Ajay Kumar Chauhan (IRS, Retd.), and ex-Indian Foreign Service High Commissioner Ruchi Ghanashyam.
